  which is what a radio group is: arrows, Tab, focus and form
  submission come from the browser, and a screen reader already knows
  how to read it. Each radio sits invisibly over its star.
- **Stars in `--warning-text`, not the amber solid.** A star that carries
  the score needs 3:1 against the page; the bright amber solid is 2.1:1 on
  white, the warning text colour 7.1:1. Empty stars use
  `--control-border`, also 3:1.
- **Read-only is one image.** "4.5 out of 5 stars" is one fact, so it is
  read once, and a fraction draws as a star filled part-way.

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.CustomText} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Unrated} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Disabled} />

  star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words with
  `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of
  the group.
- Hover previews the score up to the star under the pointer; focus shows
  the 2px ring around the star.
- Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars".
- Stars are 16px at `sm` and grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

<Meta of={SliderStories} />

# Slider

Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price
range, a brush size. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/slider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/slider).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider).

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Range} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | Optional, medium weight. Names a single thumb. |
| **Value** | Optional, after the label: the value or range, formatted, in tabular figures. |
| **Track** | `--secondary`, 6px (4px at `sm`), pill-ended. |
| **Indicator** | The filled part, `--primary-text`. |
| **Thumb** | 20px (16px at `sm`): `--background` with a 2px `--primary-text` ring. One per value. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | number, or `[number, number]` | `min` | An array makes it a range. |
| `onValueChange` | function | – | While dragging. |
| `onValueCommitted` | function | – | Once, on release. Use it for anything expensive. |
| `min`, `max`, `step` | number | `0`, `100`, `1` | |
| `largeStep` | number | `10` | Page Up / Page Down, Shift+arrows. |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `showValue` | boolean | `false` | |
| `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | – | E.g. currency, percent. |
| `thumbLabels` | string[] | – | A name per thumb, for a range. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted with a form. |
| `aria-label` | string | – | The name when there is no visible `label`. |

<Controls of={SliderStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The fill is a text colour**, as on Progress Bar: `--primary-text`
  clears 3:1 on the `--secondary` track for every accent, where the
  solid `--primary` does not.
- **The whole 20px strip is the target**, not just the 6px track: a
  press anywhere along it moves the nearest thumb there.
- **Disabled dims the control, not the words.** The label turns
  `--muted-foreground` and the value stays readable.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Steps} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Disabled} />

A slider is quick but imprecise. When the exact number matters (a price,
a quantity), pair it with a Number Input or use one instead.

## Accessibility

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` (a real range input) with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and a formatted
  `aria-valuetext`.
- A single thumb is named by `label`, or `aria-label`; a range needs
  `thumbLabels` so each thumb says which end it is.
- Keyboard: arrows move by `step`, Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrows
  by `largeStep`, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`.
- Thumbs keep their 20px size and grow a 44px hit area on coarse
  pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SwitchStories from './Switch.stories'

<Meta of={SwitchStories} />

# Switch

Turns a setting on or off, taking effect immediately. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/switch](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/switch).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch)
and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field).

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Track** | The pill. `--control-border` when off, the variant's solid when on. |
| **Thumb** | Slides to the end when on. The page colour off, the variant's label colour on. |
| **Label** | `label`. Clicking it toggles the switch. |
| **Helper text** | `helperText`, indented under the label. The error message when `validationState` is error. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | boolean | – | Controlled. |
| `defaultChecked` | boolean | `false` | The spec's `defaultValue`. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`. |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `helperText` | node | – | Not in the spec's list; see below. |
| `name` | string | – | |
| `value` | string | `"on"` | Submitted under `name` when on. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | Track 28×16, 36×20, 44×24px. |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary`, `destructive` | `primary` | Colour of the on state. |
| `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | |
| `validationState` | `default`, `success`, `error` | `default` | |

<Controls of={SwitchStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **Base UI's names:** `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` for
  the spec's `defaultValue` and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`helperText` is added.** `validationState="error"` needs somewhere to
  say what is wrong; colour alone is not a message.
- **`secondary` is a light track with a dark thumb**, not a grey version
  of the others: in this token set the secondary label is almost the
  foreground, so a dark secondary track would match `accent`.

## Usage

A switch acts at once, like a light switch. If the choice only applies
when a form is submitted, use a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Validation} />

## Accessibility

- `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it. The label wraps
  the control, so it names it and clicking it toggles it.
- The off track is `--control-border`, measured at 3:1 on the page on
  every gray ramp; the thumb is 4.5:1 or more against its track in both
  states.
- `helperText` is the switch's description (`aria-describedby`); in the
  error state the switch has `aria-invalid`.
- A hidden `<input type="checkbox">` carries `name`, `value` and
  `required` into native form submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers; the thumb stops animating
  under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AccordionStories from './Accordion.stories'

<Meta of={AccordionStories} />

# Accordion

A stack of headings that each show or hide a section of content: FAQs,
settings groups, long forms split into parts. uiguideline has no spec for
it yet, so the kit writes its own (below). Behaviour from Base UI's
[Accordion](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion).

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Container** | Frames the items (`outlined`) or leaves them edge to edge (`flush`). |
| **Item** | One heading and its panel, separated from the next by a `--border` line. |
| **Header** | A real heading element, `h3` by default (`headingLevel`). |
| **Trigger** | A button filling the header: **title** and a **chevron** that turns when open. |
| **Panel** | The content. Collapsed panels stay in the DOM for find-in-page. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `{ value, title, content, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `value` | `string[]` | – | Controlled: the open items. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | |
| `multiple` | boolean | `false` | Allow several open at once. |
| `appearance` | `outlined`, `flush` | `outlined` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | |
| `headingLevel` | `2`–`6` | `3` | |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | |

<Controls of={AccordionStories.Default} />

### Why these props

The spec is the kit's own, recorded with uiguideline's other specs:
`items` is flat, per the kit's "flat props" convention; `value` is an
array in single mode too, because that is Base UI's model and it keeps
the type the same when `multiple` is switched on; `headingLevel` exists
because a heading level must follow the page's outline, which the
component cannot know.

## Usage

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Multiple} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Flush} />

Do not hide content that most readers need; an accordion trades a
shorter page for an extra click on everything inside it.

## Accessibility

- Each trigger is a `<button>` inside a real heading, with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a region labelled by
  its trigger.
- **Every trigger is a tab stop.** Enter and Space toggle. There is no
  arrow-key movement between triggers, following the current APG
  guidance (Base UI dropped it too).
- Collapsed panels are `hidden="until-found"`: the browser's find-in-page
  reaches their text and opens the item.
- `md` triggers are 44px tall. On touch, `sm` triggers grow to 44px
  rather than overlapping each other with invisible hit areas.
- The open/close animation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories'

<Meta of={CalendarStories} />

# Calendar

A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the
inside of a Date Picker. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar).
A plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no
date library.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Header** | Previous and next month buttons around the month and year. |
| **Weekdays** | Short names, the locale's first day first. |
| **Day** | A 40px button (44px on touch). Days of the months either side are shown muted, and still pickable. |
| **Today** | A ring and bold figure. |
| **Selected** | `--primary` behind `--primary-foreground`. |
| **Unavailable** | Muted and struck through; before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by `isDateDisabled`. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | `Date` | `null` | Local midnight; times are ignored. |
| `month`, `defaultMonth`, `onMonthChange` | `Date` | value's or today's | The month shown. |
| `min`, `max` | `Date` | – | |
| `isDateDisabled` | `(date) => boolean` | – | Rule out single days. |
| `locale` | BCP 47 tag | the browser's | Month and weekday names. |
| `weekStartsOn` | 0–6 | the locale's | 0 is Sunday. |
| `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | Focus the selected day, e.g. inside a popover. |

`isSameDay`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay` and `firstDayOfWeek`
are exported for working with the same plain dates.

<Controls of={CalendarStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Six rows always.** Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height
  keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them.
- **The locale decides the week.** `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday,
  `en-US` on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it
  (Monday otherwise).
- **Month steps keep the day where they can.** 31 January plus a month
  is 28 February, not 3 March.

  <Canvas of={CalendarStories.MonthEnds} />

## Usage

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MinMax} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.NoWeekends} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Vietnamese} />

## Accessibility

- A `role="grid"` named by the month and year, with column headers
  carrying the full weekday name. The selected cell has
  `aria-selected`, today's day `aria-current="date"`, and each day
  button the full date as its name ("Friday 18 September 2026").
- One tab stop: the selected day (or today). Arrows move a day or a
  week, Home and End go to the week's ends, Page Up and Page Down move a
  month and Shift+Page Up/Down a year, Enter or Space selects. Moving
  past the month shows the next one.

  <Canvas of={CalendarStories.Keyboard} />

- The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced.
- Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are
  found and announced as unavailable rather than skipped silently.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CardStories from './Card.stories'

<Meta of={CardStories} />

# Card

A surface that groups related content: a summary, a person, a setting.
Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/card](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/card).

<Canvas of={CardStories.Appearances} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Container** | The surface: `--card` (elevated, outline) or `--surface-subtle` (filled), padded by `size`. |
| **Border** | `--border`, the non-interactive one. `hasBorder` turns it off. |
| **Content** | `children`, stacked or side by side (`orientation`). |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | node | – | The spec's `content`. |
| `size` | `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `sm` | Padding 12, 16, 24, 32px; gap between children scales with it. |
| `appearance` | `elevated`, `outline`, `filled`, `unstyled` | `elevated` | |
| `orientation` | `vertical`, `horizontal` | `vertical` | |
| `isRounded` | boolean | `true` | `--radius-panel`. |
| `hasBorder` | boolean | `true` | |
| `onClick` | function | – | Makes the card a `<button>`. |
| `render` | element or function | – | E.g. `<a href>` for a card that navigates. |

<Controls of={CardStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **`children`, not `content`.** Arbitrary content is what React children
  are for.
- **`orientation` defaults to `vertical`.** The spec says `horizontal`,
  which would lay a title and its description side by side.
- **`render` is added** so a card can be a link, alongside `onClick` for
  a card that acts.
- **`filled` uses `--surface-subtle`**, not `--muted`: muted text reads
  4.81:1 on it against 4.60:1 on `--muted`, and it stays a step off
  `--card` so the fill still reads.
- **`unstyled`** keeps the padding and layout and drops every visual.

## Usage

<Canvas of={CardStories.Horizontal} />

<Canvas of={CardStories.Clickable} />

## Accessibility

- A plain card is a `<div>` and adds nothing to the accessibility tree.
- **A clickable card is one `<button>`, so everything inside becomes its
  label.** A button may only hold phrasing content: use spans for its
  title and text, not headings or paragraphs, and put no links or buttons
  inside it — nested interactive content is invalid and unreachable. If a card needs its own
  actions, leave it plain and put a button in it (the Horizontal story).
- A card that navigates should be a link (`render={<a href>}`), not a
  button with a click handler.
- Put headings inside at the level the page needs; the card has none of
  its own.
- Muted text clears 4.5:1 on every appearance, at rest and on hover:
  hover changes the shadow or the edge, never the surface under the text.

<Meta of={CarouselStories} />

# Carousel

A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery,
onboarding cards. Everything in it is hidden until the reader goes
looking, so use it for content that is fine to miss; a list or a grid
shows more at once. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/carousel](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/carousel).
A native scrolling track with snap points, following the
[WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/).

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Controls** | Previous and next, plus stop/start when it rotates. Above the track, at its end, so they never cover a slide. |
| **Track** | A horizontal scroller with snap points. Swipe, trackpad and arrow keys scroll it natively. |
| **Slide** | One child. Labelled "2 of 5". |
| **Dots** | One per stop. The current one is a wider bar. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | nodes | – | One per slide. |
| `label` | string | – | Required. Names the carousel. |
| `slidesPerView` | number | `1` | Slides in view at once. |
| `showDots` | boolean | `true` | |
| `loop` | boolean | `false` | Previous and next wrap at the ends. |
| `autoPlay` | number (ms) | – | Advance on a timer. See Accessibility. |
| `index` | number | – | Controlled: the first slide in view. |
| `defaultIndex` | number | `0` | |
| `onIndexChange` | `(index) => void` | – | Called for buttons, dots, swipes and the timer. |

<Controls of={CarouselStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Native scrolling.** No transform maths and no gesture library: the
  track is `overflow-x: auto` with `scroll-snap-type`, so touch, trackpad
  and momentum behave as the platform does. The index is read back once
  the track comes to rest.
- **Stops, not slides.** With three in view, five slides have three stops
  (1-3, 2-4, 3-5), and the dots count stops.
- **Right to left works.** Offsets are measured from the first slide, so
  the negative `scrollLeft` of an RTL track reads correctly, and the
  previous/next chevrons are mirrored.
- **`defaultIndex` starts there.** The track jumps to it on mount, without
  a scroll animation.

## Usage

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.ThreeInView} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Loop} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.AutoPlay} />

## Accessibility

- A `<section>` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and your `label`;
  each slide is a group with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and a name
  like "2 of 5".
- **Autoplay** (WCAG 2.2.2) pauses while the pointer is over the carousel
  or focus is inside it, has a stop/start button as its first control, and
  never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- A visually hidden line says where you are ("Slide 3 of 5", or "Slides
  2 to 4 of 5"). It is `aria-live="polite"` when the reader moves the
  carousel, so a screen reader hears the change, and `off` while it
  rotates on its own. The slides themselves never change in the DOM, so a
  live region round them would stay silent.
- Previous and next are disabled at the ends unless `loop`. Dots are
  buttons named "Slide 3" with `aria-current` on the current stop.
- The track is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so a keyboard can scroll it,
  and shows the 2px `--ring`. Buttons and dots have 44px touch targets on
  coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CollapseStories from './Collapse.stories'

<Meta of={CollapseStories} />

# Collapse

One show/hide section: "Show details", "Advanced settings". A text button
with a chevron, and the content it reveals under it. For a list of
sections, use an [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-data-display-accordion--docs).
Our own spec: uiguideline.com has no page for it. Behaviour from Base
UI's [Collapsible](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible).

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Open} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | A medium-weight text button, underlined on hover, with a chevron that turns from right to down. |
| **Panel** | The content, 8px under the trigger. Its height animates open and shut. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | node | – | Required. The trigger's text. |
| `openLabel` | node | `label` | The trigger's text while open, e.g. "Hide details". |
| `children` | node | – | Required. |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | `body-sm` or `body`. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | boolean | `true` | Closed content stays findable. |

<Controls of={CollapseStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **A text button, not a bar.** Accordion items are full-width bars with
  dividers because they are the page's structure; a Collapse is one
  aside in running content, so its trigger reads like a link in a
  sentence.
- **Findable when closed.** By default closed content is kept as
  `hidden="until-found"`: the browser's find-in-page still matches it and
  opens the section. Turn it off only for content that is expensive to
  render.

## Usage

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`
  pointing at the panel.
- Enter or Space toggles it. With `openLabel`, the button's name changes
  with its state ("Show details" / "Hide details"), and `aria-expanded`
  says it either way.
- The chevron is decorative. The trigger grows to a 44px target on
  coarse pointers.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the panel and chevron change without
  animating.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TableStories from './Table.stories'

<Meta of={TableStories} />

# Table

Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects,
invoices, members. Columns can sort, rows can be selected. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/table](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/table).
A native `<table>`; selection uses the kit's Checkbox.

<Canvas of={TableStories.Selectable} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Caption** | Names the table. Visually hidden unless `showCaption`. |
| **Header row** | `--surface-subtle`, small muted labels. Sortable headers are buttons with a sort icon. |
| **Row** | 48px (40px at `sm`), divided by `--border`. |
| **Row header** | The column marked `isRowHeader`, medium weight: the name a row is known by. |
| **Selection column** | Optional checkboxes; the header one selects all and shows "mixed". |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `TableColumn[]` | – | Required. `{ key, header, cell?, sortable?, sortValue?, align?, width?, isRowHeader? }` |
| `rows` | array | – | Required. |
| `caption` | node | – | Required. |
| `showCaption` | boolean | `false` | |
| `getRowId` | `(row, index) => string` | index | Needed for selection that survives re-sorting and paging. |
| `sort`, `defaultSort`, `onSortChange` | `{ key, direction } \| null` | `null` | Controlled sort leaves the sorting to you. |
| `isSelectable` | boolean | `false` | |
| `selectedIds`, `defaultSelectedIds`, `onSelectionChange` | string[] | `[]` | |
| `density` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | |
| `hasStickyHeader` | boolean | `false` | Header stays in view while the container scrolls. |
| `emptyState` | node | – | Shown when there are no rows. |

<Controls of={TableStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Numbers align to the end, in tabular figures,** so digits line up
  column-wide. Set `align: 'end'` on every numeric or date column.
- **Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to
  the original order, which is often the one that meant something.
  Uncontrolled, the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as
  numbers, text by locale with "file 2" before "file 10".
- **Paging is not built in.** Put a Pagination under the table and pass
  it one page of `rows`; with `getRowId`, selection keeps working across
  pages.

## Usage

<Canvas of={TableStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.Compact} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.Empty} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.StickyHeader} />

With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back
the rows already sorted:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ControlledSort} />

## Accessibility

- A real `<table>` with a `<caption>`, `<th scope="col">` headers and a
  `<th scope="row">` for the row header column: screen readers announce
  the column and row for every cell.
- Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or
  `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header.
- Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"); the
  header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports `mixed` when some are
  selected.
- The table scrolls sideways inside its container on narrow screens
  instead of squeezing columns.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ComboboxStories from './Combobox.stories'

<Meta of={ComboboxStories} />

# Combobox

A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one.
Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox).

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | `label`. |
| **Combobox input** | A text input; typing filters the list. |
| **Clean button** | "Clear selection", when `isClearable`. |
| **Open button** | "Show options": the chevron. Opens the full list. |
| **Options list** | Filtered as you type; "No matches" when empty, "Loading…" while loading. |
| **Option (matched)** | The typed text is marked in each option. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `string[]` or `{ value, label, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. Labels are strings: they are typed and matched. |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | string or `null` | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`; `null` when cleared. |
| `isClearable` | boolean | `true` | |
| `emptyText` | string | `"No matches"` | |
| `placeholder`, `label`, `helperText`, `validationState` | | – | |
| `size`, `appearance`, `isFullWidth` | | | As on Text Input. |
| `isLoading` | boolean | `false` | Spinner in the field and "Loading…" in the list. |
| `name` | string | – | Submits the option's value. |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | |

<Controls of={ComboboxStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **Labels must be strings**, not components: they are what is typed,
  matched and shown in the input.
- **`emptyText`** is added: an empty list needs to say why.
- `onValueChange` and native names, as on Select.

## Usage

For long lists, or when people already know what they are looking for.
It chooses from the list only; free text that is not an option is not a
value.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Clear} />

## Accessibility

- The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox`.
- **Keyboard:** typing opens and filters; the first match is highlighted
  so Enter picks it; Up and Down move; Escape closes, then clears.
- The match is marked by weight and underline, not colour, so it keeps
  the option's full contrast on the highlighted row.
- The open button is named "Show options" and is out of the tab order
  (the input already opens the list); the clear button is "Clear
  selection".
- Loading and empty states are announced from the list.

<Meta of={DatePickerStories} />

# Date Picker

A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker).
Built from the kit's field, Base UI's
[Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) and
[Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs).

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

The field's parts (label, box, helper), plus:

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Input** | Typed date in the locale's numeric order: `dd/mm/yyyy` in `en-GB` and `vi-VN`, `mm/dd/yyyy` in `en-US`. |
| **Calendar button** | Opens the calendar in a popover, aligned to the field's end. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | `Date \| null` | `null` | `null` when cleared. |
| `label`, `helperText`, `validationState` | | | As on Text Input. |
| `size`, `appearance`, `isFullWidth` | | `md`, `outlined` | As on Text Input. |
| `min`, `max`, `isDateDisabled` | | – | Passed to the calendar and checked when typing. |
| `locale`, `weekStartsOn` | | the browser's | |
| `placeholder` | string | the locale's pattern | |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd`. |
| `disabled`, `required` | boolean | `false` | |

<Controls of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Typing is first-class.** Many people type a known date faster than
  they can page to it. Any separator works (`3.10.26`, `3/10/2026`); the
  field reformats on blur or Enter.
- **An impossible date is kept, not guessed.** `31/02/2026` stays as
  typed, the field turns to its error state and the helper shows the
  expected pattern; nothing is reported until it is a real date.
- **The form gets ISO.** Whatever the display order, `name` submits
  `yyyy-mm-dd`, so the server never has to guess the locale.

## Usage

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Typing} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.UnitedStates} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Range} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

- The input is a labelled text box with `inputmode="numeric"` for a
  number keypad; while the text is not a valid date it has
  `aria-invalid` and the helper explains the format.
- The calendar button is named "Choose date", with the current date when
  there is one. Alt+Down in the input opens it too.
- The calendar opens as a dialog with focus on the selected day; picking
  a day closes it and returns focus to the button, Escape closes it
  without a change.
- The field and calendar's own labels ("Choose date", "Previous month")
  are in English, like the rest of the kit's built-in labels.

<Meta of={FileUploaderStories} />

# File Uploader

Choose files to send: drag them onto the drop zone or pick them with the
button. It checks type, size and count, lists what was chosen, and shows
progress or an error per file. It does not upload: your code does, and
tells it how that is going. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader).
A native `<input type="file">` behind a kit Button.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.WithStatus} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | Names the whole uploader (a group). |
| **Drop zone** | A dashed area with an icon, "Drag files here or", and the Choose button. Solid-edged while a file is over it. |
| **Choose button** | Opens the system picker. The way in for keyboard, screen reader and touch. |
| **Helper text** | What is allowed, e.g. "PDF, PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB each." |
| **Errors** | One line per file that was not added, in `--danger-text`. |
| **File list** | Name, size, optional progress bar or error, and a remove button. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `File[]` | – | Controlled. |
| `defaultFiles` | `File[]` | `[]` | |
| `onFilesChange` | `(files) => void` | – | After an add or a remove. |
| `onReject` | `(rejections) => void` | – | `{ file, reason: 'type' \| 'size' \| 'count', message }[]`. |
| `accept` | string | – | As the native attribute: `.pdf,image/*`. Checked on drop too. |
| `multiple` | boolean | `false` | One file is replaced by the next; many are appended. |

  new file replaces the chosen one only if it passes the checks.

  match, so it is skipped rather than listed again.

  moves to the next file's button, or back to Choose when the list is
  empty, so it is never lost.

# Number Input

A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/number-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/number-input).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field);
the field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Input** | The number, in tabular figures, formatted to `precision`. |
| **Decrease button** | `minus`. Disabled at `min`. |
| **Increase button** | `plus`. Disabled at `max`. |

Plus the shared **label** and **helper text**.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number or `null` | – | Controlled; `null` is empty. |
| `defaultValue` | number | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`; `null` when emptied. |
| `min`, `max` | number | – | |
| `step` | number | `1` | Buttons and arrow keys. Shift steps by 10, Alt by 0.1. |
| `precision` | number | – | Decimal places shown and accepted. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | |
| `appearance` | `outlined`, `filled`, `underlined`, `unstyled` | `outlined` | |
| `label`, `helperText`, `validationState` | | – | From the shared field. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |
| `name`, `placeholder` | string | – | |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required` | boolean | `false` | Native names. |

<Controls of={NumberInputStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **`onValueChange` with a number**, not `onChange`: built on Base UI, it
  takes Base UI's name, and the value arrives parsed rather than as text.
- **`max` is optional with no default.** The spec marks it required with a
  default of 100, which contradicts itself; a quantity with no upper
  bound is common.
- **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`, `appearance`** are added
  from the shared field.

## Usage

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Precision} />

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Sizes} />

Use it for quantities people adjust by a little. For numbers that are
really identifiers — card numbers, postcodes, phone numbers — use a Text
Input with `inputMode="numeric"`: stepping a postcode is meaningless.

## Accessibility

- The input is a text field with `inputmode="numeric"` and the role
  description "Number field"; Up and Down step it, Shift and Alt change
  the step, Home and End go to `min` and `max`.
- The buttons are named Increase and Decrease and are disabled at the
  limits, so a screen reader hears why nothing happened.
- The value is parsed and formatted in the user's locale.
- Stepper buttons widen to 44px on touch screens.

A field for a search query, with a button to clear it. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/search](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/search).

| **Input** | `type="search"`. |
| **Placeholder** | "Search" unless given. |
| **Clean button** | "Clear search": shown while there is text, hidden when disabled or read-only. |

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | string | `''` | |
| `onChange` | `(event) => void` | – | Native event, including when cleared. |

| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |

  so a search box can match the form or toolbar it sits in.
- **`value` is added** for a controlled query.
- Native `disabled`, `readOnly` names.

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Sizes} />

searches the site, so it becomes a landmark. The component is only the
field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark.

  or "Search". A placeholder is not a name.
- **Clearing works the same everywhere:** the button, and Escape in the
  field (Chrome and Safari do this natively; Firefox did not). Either way
  `onChange` fires with a real event and focus stays in the field.

  not two.

<Meta of={SelectStories} />

# Select

Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/select](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/select).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select);
the field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Appearances} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | `label`. Clicking it focuses the field without opening it. |
| **Select input** | A button showing the selected label or the placeholder, and a chevron (a spinner while loading). |
| **Options list** | Opens below the field, in a portal. |
| **Option** | Each option; the selected one has a check. Disabled options are dimmed and skipped. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `string[]` or `{ value, label, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. Labels may be nodes. |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | string or `null` | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`. |
| `placeholder` | string | – | Shown until something is chosen. |
| `label`, `helperText`, `validationState` | | – | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | |
| `appearance` | `outlined`, `filled`, `underlined`, `unstyled` | `outlined` | |
| `isLoading` | boolean | `false` | Spinner in place of the chevron; `aria-busy`. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted with the form. |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | Native names. |

<Controls of={SelectStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **`onValueChange` with the value**, Base UI's name, instead of
  `onChange`.
- **Native names** for `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`.
- **Options are strings or `{ value, label }` objects.** A bare component
  is not an option: an option needs a value to submit and compare, so a
  component goes in `label`.
- **The list opens below the field** instead of Base UI's default of
  laying it over the trigger with the selected option aligned — the
  anatomy shows a list below.

## Usage

Five to about fifteen options. Fewer: radios, which show every choice at
once. More, or when people know what they want: a
[Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs), which lets them
type.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Sizes} />

## Accessibility

- The field is a button with `role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`
  and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` of `option`s.
- **Keyboard:** Space, Enter or Up/Down open it; arrows move, typing
  jumps to a matching option, Enter selects, Escape closes, and focus
  returns to the field.
- **Read-only** locks the value, not the list: it still opens so the
  options can be read, but choosing one changes nothing. The field has
  `aria-readonly`. Use `disabled` when the list should not open at all.
- The label is associated with the field (it is a `<div>` because a
  `<label>` would also click the button).
- The list renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`: it reads the
  root's tokens, so a `Theme` scope around the field does not restyle it.
- Options are 32px, 44px on touch screens.

# Text Input

A single line of text: a name, an email, a URL. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/text-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/text-input).
Label, description and invalid state are wired by Base UI's
[Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field).

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Appearances} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | `label`, above the field. Clicking it focuses the input. |
| **Field** | The box that draws the edge, fill and focus ring. |
| **Prefix** / **Suffix** | `prefix`, `suffix`: text or an icon inside the field, in the muted colour. |
| **Placeholder** | `placeholder`. A hint, never a replacement for the label. |
| **Helper text** | `helperText`, under the field. The error message when `validationState` is error. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `helperText` | node | – | |
| `validationState` | `default`, `success`, `error` | `default` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | 32, 40, 48px. |
| `appearance` | `outlined`, `filled`, `underlined`, `unstyled` | `outlined` | |
| `prefix`, `suffix` | node | – | |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Otherwise 20rem, capped at its container. |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange` | | – | As on `<input>`: `onChange` gets the event. |
| `placeholder`, `name`, `pattern`, `maxLength`, `type`, `autoFocus` | | – | Native. |
| `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Native. |

Every other `<input>` attribute passes through to the input, including `ref`.

<Controls of={TextInputStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **Native names** for native attributes: `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` rather than `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`onChange` is the native event**, not a value: the kit's rule for
  components that wrap a real input, so it works with every form library
  as-is.
- **Changed in 0.8:** `error` became `validationState="error"` plus
  `helperText`; `forwardRef` is gone (`ref` is a prop in React 19).

## Usage

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.PrefixSuffix} />

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Validation} />

Pick one appearance per form. `outlined` is the default; `filled` suits
dense settings pages; `underlined` and `unstyled` are for fields that sit
inside something else that already draws the edge.

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the input; the helper is its
  description (`aria-describedby`); the error state sets `aria-invalid`.
  Do not rely on the placeholder as a label: it disappears as soon as
  anyone types.
- **The edge is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page**, because WCAG
  1.4.11 applies to a text field's boundary. The lighter `--input` token
  is about 1.3:1.
- Focus draws a 2px ring around the whole field (in the danger colour
  when invalid), on click as well as keyboard, since that is where typing
  goes.
- Pressing the field's padding or a prefix focuses the input, like a
  native field.
- Heights are 32–48px; the label is part of the target too.

# Textarea

Several lines of text: a message, a description, a note. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/textarea](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/textarea).
The same field as [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs):
label, helper, validation, sizes and appearances are shared.

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.Appearances} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | `label`, above the field. |
| **Field** | The box: edge, fill and focus ring, padded top and bottom so it grows with the text. |
| **Placeholder** | `placeholder`. |
| **Resize handle** | The browser's own, on the axes `resize` allows. Hidden with `hasAutoSize`. |
| **Helper text** | `helperText`; the error message when `validationState` is error. |

## Props

Everything Text Input takes except `prefix` and `suffix`, plus:

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resize` | `none`, `both`, `vertical`, `horizontal` | `vertical` | |
| `hasAutoSize` | boolean | `false` | Grows and shrinks with the text. |
| `minRows` | number | `3` | Starting height (the `rows` attribute). |
| `maxRows` | number | – | Where auto-size stops and scrolling starts. |

`onChange` is the native event; every other `<textarea>` attribute passes
through, including `ref`.

<Controls of={TextareaStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- Native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` names, and native `onChange`,
  as on Text Input.
- **`minRows` defaults to 3.** The spec gives none; the browser's own
  default of 2 is too short to read as a multi-line field.

## Usage

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.AutoSize} />

Use auto-size for text whose length varies a lot, with a `maxRows` so the
page does not grow without limit. Keep the manual handle (`vertical`) when
people may want to see more at once.

## Accessibility

- A real `<textarea>` with its `<label>`, the helper as its description,
  and `aria-invalid` in the error state.
- Edge at 3:1 on the page (`--control-border`); focus ring around the
  whole field.
- Enter inserts a line break; it does not submit the form.
- Auto-size caps at `maxRows` and scrolls beyond it, so a long entry never
  pushes the rest of the form off screen.

| **Track** | The full length, `--secondary`. |
| **Indicator** | The filled share, coloured by `variant`. A sliding third when indeterminate. |
| **Value label** | `showValueLabel`: the percentage after the bar, in tabular figures. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | `0` | |
| `max` | number | `100` | The spec's `maxValue`. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | Track height 4, 8, 12px. |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary`, `destructive` | `primary` | Colour of the fill. |
| `isRounded` | boolean | `false` | Pill ends on track and fill. |
| `isIndeterminate` | boolean | `false` | Progress with no known amount. |
| `showValueLabel` | boolean | `false` | Hidden while indeterminate. |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `aria-label` | string | – | The name when there is no visible `label`. |

Any other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`, `aria-labelledby`,
`min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`.

<Controls of={ProgressBarStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native
  `<progress>` use.

### Design notes

- **The fill is a text colour, not a solid.** The fill is what carries
  the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the track, and some accent
  solids do not: amber's is about 2.9:1 on white. So `primary` fills with
  `--primary-text`, `accent` with `--foreground`, `secondary` with
  `--muted-foreground` and `destructive` with `--danger-text`, each a
  colour meant to be read as text on the page, which keeps it at 3:1 or
  more on the track.

## Usage

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.ValueLabel} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Sizes} />

`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Max} />

When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate
and switch to a value as soon as there is one.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Indeterminate} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and
  `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops
  `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0.
- Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or
  `aria-label`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both
  modes. The value label is `--muted-foreground`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops animating between values
  and the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass.
- A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it
  (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SkeletonStories from './Skeleton.stories'

<Meta of={SkeletonStories} />

# Skeleton

A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page
keeps its layout and the reader sees what is coming. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/skeleton](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/skeleton).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.CardPlaceholder} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Bone** | One shape, `--muted`: a line of text, an avatar, an image. |
| **Rows** | With `rows`, a stack of bones with the last one at 60%, like the end of a paragraph. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | number or string | 100% (circle 40px) | A number is px; a string any CSS length. |
| `height` | number or string | 16px | Of each row, with `rows`. Ignored by a single circle. |
| `appearance` | `circle`, `square`, `rounded` | `square` | A circle takes its height from its width; with `rows` it draws rounded bars. |
| `rows` | number | – | Stacked lines, 8px apart. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Overrides `width`. |
| `hasAnimation` | boolean | `false` | A slow pulse. |

Any other prop goes to the outer `<div>`.

<Controls of={SkeletonStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **`hasAnimation` is off by default.** A screen of pulsing shapes is
  noise; animate the few that matter, or none.
- **`rows` shortens the last line**, which reads as text rather than as a
  block.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Appearances} />

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Rows} />

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Animated} />

Match the shapes to the content that will replace them: same sizes,
same gaps. A skeleton that jumps to a different layout on load is worse
than a spinner. For content whose shape is unknown, use a
[Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).

## Accessibility

- **A skeleton is decoration** and is `aria-hidden`. It says nothing to
  a screen reader, so the region it stands in for has to: put
  `aria-busy="true"` on it (as the CardPlaceholder story does) and remove
  it when the content arrives.
- If the wait matters, announce it: a visually hidden status, or a
  Spinner with a label.
- `--muted` is below any contrast floor on purpose. It is not content,
  and should not compete with content that has arrived.
- The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories'

<Meta of={SpinnerStories} />

# Spinner

Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will
take, or, given a value, how far along it is. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner).
A plain element: there is no behaviour here worth Base UI.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Track** | The full circle, `--border`. Frames the motion; decoration. |
| **Indicator** | The arc: a quarter turn spinning, or the value as a share of the ring. Coloured by `variant`. |
| **Label** | `label`, under the indicator. Also the accessible name. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | 16, 24, 32px. |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary` | `accent` | Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button. |
| `label` | string | – | Visible text and accessible name; `"Loading"` when omitted or empty. |
| `delay` | number (ms) | `0` | Renders nothing until it has passed. |
| `value` | 0–100 | – | Turns it into a progress ring. Clamped. |
| `isIndeterminate` | boolean | `false` | Spin even when `value` is given. |

Any other prop goes to the outer `<span>`.

<Controls of={SpinnerStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **`accent` is the default variant**, in `--foreground`: a spinner is
  most often a quiet placeholder inside content that has its own colour.
- **`value`**: A load that can report progress should, and a
  ring reads better than a bar in a small space such as a button or a
  thumbnail.
- **`delay`**: Most loads finish in under half a second; a
  spinner that appears and vanishes in 200ms is a flash, not information.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Determinate} />

Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner
only appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Delay} />

For a load of a page region whose shape you know, a
[Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) says more. For
a long task with a known size, use a
[Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).

## Accessibility

- **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by
  `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the
  label, or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once
  `delay` has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region
  that is already in the page, not a region that mounts full.
- **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`,
  `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`.
- The SVG is hidden.
- The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--primary-text`
  (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--muted-foreground`, `--foreground`.
  The track is decoration and may be faint.
- The progress ring's transition stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than
  stopping: a frozen arc reads as "stuck".
- Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the
  spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as BreadcrumbsStories from './Breadcrumbs.stories'

<Meta of={BreadcrumbsStories} />

# Breadcrumbs

The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each
step a link back up. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Link** | Each level above the current page, `--muted-foreground`, underlined on hover. |
| **Separator** | A chevron (or any node), decorative. |
| **Current page** | The last item, `--foreground`, medium weight, not a link. |
| **Ellipsis** | With `maxItems`, a button standing in for the collapsed middle. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `{ label, href?, render? }[]` | – | Required. Top level first; the last is the current page. |
| `maxItems` | number (2 or more) | – | Collapse the middle beyond this many. |
| `separator` | node | chevron | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | `body-sm` or `body`. |
| `aria-label` | string | `Breadcrumb` | The landmark's name. |

`render` on an item replaces its `<a>`, e.g. with a router's link. Every
other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={BreadcrumbsStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Muted links, underlined on hover.** The trail is obviously a row of
  links, so it can drop the permanent underline that links in running
  text keep; the current page stands out by colour and weight instead.
- **The current page is not a link.** A link to the page you are on does
  nothing useful and reads as one more place to go.

## Usage

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Collapsed} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.CustomSeparator} />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb", around an ordered list: screen
  readers announce "list, 4 items" and the position of each.
- The last item has `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators are `aria-hidden`, so they are not read between items.
- The ellipsis is a button named "Show 3 more". Pressing it expands the
  trail and moves focus to the first item it revealed.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as LinkStories from './Link.stories'

<Meta of={LinkStories} />

# Link

Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an
outside site. It navigates; it does not act. For an action, use a
[Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/link](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/link).

<Canvas of={LinkStories.InText} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Text** | The link's name. Say where it goes ("See pricing"), not "click here". |
| **Underline** | 1px, thickening to 2px on hover. |
| **External icon** | With `isExternal`: an arrow out of a box, plus "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | string | – | |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary` | `primary` | Colour. `accent` is the foreground. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | – | Omitted, it inherits the size of the text around it. |
| `underline` | `always`, `hover` | `always` | See below. |
| `isExternal` | boolean | `false` | New tab, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, icon and announcement. |
| `isDisabled` | boolean | `false` | Drops `href`, sets `aria-disabled`. |
| `render` | element or function | – | Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link />`. |

Every other `<a>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

<Controls of={LinkStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Underlined by default.** Colour alone does not mark a link for
  someone who cannot tell the colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1), so a link in
  running text keeps its line. `underline="hover"` is for places where
  the context already says "these are links": a nav list, a footer
  column.
- **Hover thickens the line, it does not change the colour.** Every
  variant is a text colour measured at 4.5:1; a hover colour would need
  measuring again for every accent and mode.
- **No `visited` style.** Most links in an app lead to screens, not
  documents, and a purple "seen it" marker there is noise.

## Usage

<Canvas of={LinkStories.Variants} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.UnderlineOnHover} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.External} />

With a router, pass its link as `render`. Link merges its class and props
onto it, and the router keeps control of navigation:

```tsx
<Link render={<RouterLink to="/settings" />}>Settings</Link>
```

## Accessibility

- A real `<a href>`, so it is in the tab order, opens with Enter, and
  shows up in a screen reader's list of links.
- `isExternal` adds "(opens in a new tab)" to the accessible name: a new
  tab that opens without warning strands people who cannot see it happen.
- `isDisabled` removes `href`, the only thing that stops an `<a>`
  navigating, and marks it `aria-disabled`. Without an `href` it leaves
  the tab order. Prefer hiding a link that cannot be followed, or saying
  in text why it is unavailable.
- Focus shows a 2px `--ring` outline, offset 2px.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories'

<Meta of={MenuStories} />

# Menu

A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an
"Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick
a value for a form, use a Select. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | `trigger`: one button. Menu merges its props onto it. |
| **Popup** | The Select list's surface: `--popover`, border, `--shadow-md`, `--radius-field`, at least 12rem wide. |
| **Item** | Icon (optional), label, shortcut (optional). 32px tall, 44px on touch. |
| **Checkbox / radio item** | A check or a dot in the icon column. They do not close the menu. |
| **Submenu trigger** | An item with `items`, and a chevron. |
| **Group label**, **separator** | Structure for longer menus. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | element | – | Required. |
| `items` | `MenuEntry[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `side` | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` | `bottom` | |
| `align` | `start`, `center`, `end` | `start` | |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |

<Controls of={MenuStories.Default} />

`items` is data, like Select's `options`. Each entry is one of:

| `type` | Fields | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omitted or `'item'` | `label`, `onSelect`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `isDestructive`, `disabled`, `href`, `items` | `href` makes it a link; `items` makes it a submenu. |
| `'checkbox'` | `label`, `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `disabled` | |
| `'radio'` | `label`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `options` | One labelled group of radio items. |
| `'group'` | `label`, `items` | A labelled group. |
| `'separator'` | | |

Give a `textValue` when `label` is not plain text, for typeahead.

### Design notes

- **Destructive items use the danger text colour**, on a `--danger-subtle`
  highlight, both at 4.5:1. Put them last, after a separator.
- **Toggles keep the menu open**, so several can be changed in one go;
  actions close it.
- **Shortcuts are display only.** `shortcut` shows "⌘ D"; binding the
  key is up to the page.

## Usage

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Groups} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Submenu} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Links} />

## Accessibility

- The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup
  is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and
  `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and
  `aria-disabled` on disabled items.
- Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows
  move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the
  matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow
  Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names
  the item.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories'

<Meta of={PaginationStories} />

# Pagination

Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the
page numbers around the current one. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Middle} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Previous / Next** | Chevron buttons, disabled at either end. |
| **Page** | A square ghost button with the number, tabular figures. |
| **Current page** | The only solid: `--primary` behind `--primary-foreground`. |
| **Ellipsis** | "…" where two or more pages are skipped. Decorative. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `totalPages` | number | – | Required. |
| `page`, `defaultPage`, `onPageChange` | number (1-based) | `1` | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `siblingCount` | number | `1` | Pages shown either side of the current one. |
| `boundaryCount` | number | `1` | Pages always shown at each end. |

  current page keeps a sibling each side, and a "…" appears only where
  it hides two or more pages: a single hidden page is shown instead,
  since "…" would take the same room. The number of controls stays the
  same as you move through the middle, so the Next button does not jump.

import * as SidebarStories from './Sidebar.stories'

<Meta of={SidebarStories} />

# Sidebar

The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen: a header,
links in named groups, and a footer. It can collapse to an icon rail.
Our own spec: uiguideline.com has no page for it. A plain element; the
rail's labels use [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs).

<Canvas of={SidebarStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Header** | Optional: the product name, a workspace switcher. The collapse button sits here. |
| **Item** | Icon, label and optional badge, a 40px row (44px on touch). |
| **Current item** | Lifted onto `--background` with a `--control-border` edge and medium weight, like a selected pill tab. |
| **Group** | A small muted label over its items. In the rail, a rule. |
| **Footer** | Optional, pinned to the bottom: the signed-in user, help. Hidden in the rail. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SidebarEntry[]` | – | Required. Items `{ label, href, icon?, badge?, render? }` and groups `{ type: 'group', label, items }`. |
| `currentHref` | string | – | That item gets `aria-current="page"`. |
| `header`, `footer` | node | – | |
| `isCollapsed`, `defaultCollapsed`, `onCollapsedChange` | boolean | `false` | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `isCollapsible` | boolean | `false` | Show the collapse button. |
| `aria-label` | string | `Main` | The landmark's name. |

`render` on an item replaces its `<a>`, e.g. with a router's link. Every
other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={SidebarStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The current page is lifted, not just tinted.** The sidebar sits on
  `--surface-subtle`, one grey step from a hover fill, so the current
  item gets the selected-pill treatment used by Tabs: background, edge
  and weight.
- **Group names are labels, not headings.** They name their list
  ("Projects, list, 3 items") without adding `<h2>`s that would compete
  with the page's own outline.
- **The rail needs an icon on every item.** Collapsed, the label moves
  into a tooltip on hover and focus, and stays the link's name.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SidebarStories.Collapsible} />

<Canvas of={SidebarStories.Plain} />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Main". The current item has
  `aria-current="page"`.
- Each group's label names its list through `aria-labelledby`, and
  keeps doing so in the rail, where it is only visually hidden.
- In the rail each link keeps its name through `aria-label`, badge
  included ("Inbox, 12"), and a tooltip shows the same text on hover
  and keyboard focus.
- The collapse button is named "Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar"
  and carries `aria-expanded`.

import * as StepperStories from './Stepper.stories'

<Meta of={StepperStories} />

# Stepper

Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up,
checkout, a setup wizard. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Marker** | A 32px disc (24px at `sm`): a check when complete, the number when current (primary ring) or upcoming (grey ring), a warning icon on error. |
| **Label** | Medium weight; muted for upcoming steps, danger for an error. |
| **Description** | Optional, small, muted. |
| **Connector** | The line to the next step: primary once the step is complete, `--border` ahead. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `{ label, description?, status? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `current` | number (0-based) | – | Required. Earlier steps are complete. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | |
| `onStepClick` | `(index) => void` | – | Makes finished and current steps buttons. |
| `aria-label` | string | `Progress` | The landmark's name. |

A step's `status` (`complete`, `current`, `upcoming`, `error`) overrides
the one worked out from `current`. Every other `<nav>` attribute passes
through.

<Controls of={StepperStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Horizontal puts the text under the marker**, so the connectors run
  marker to marker and every step gets the same width whatever the
  length of its label. Use vertical when the steps have long
  descriptions, or in a narrow sidebar.
- **Only finished steps can be revisited.** With `onStepClick`, complete
  and current steps become buttons; upcoming ones stay text, because a
  flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs.
- **Complete is filled, current is ringed.** Both use the primary
  colour; the fill says "done", the ring says "you are here".

## Usage

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Navigable} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.WithError} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Small} />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen
  readers announce the number of steps and the position of each.
- The current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in
  visually hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started",
  "Workspace, has an error".
- With `onStepClick`, the clickable steps are real buttons with the
  focus ring, and grow to 44px on coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories'

<Meta of={TabsStories} />

# Tabs

Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page:
Overview, Activity, Settings of one project. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/tabs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tabs).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs).

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Tab list** | The row (or column) of tabs. |
| **Tab** | Optional icon and a label, medium weight. `--muted-foreground` until selected (`--foreground` on pills). |
| **Indicator** | `underline`: a 2px `--foreground` bar that slides to the selected tab. `pills`: a `--background` segment with a `--control-border` edge. |
| **Panel** | The selected tab's `content`. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `{ value, label, content?, icon?, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | string | first enabled | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `appearance` | `underline`, `pills` | `underline` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 32 or 40px tabs. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Tabs share the width equally. |
| `activateOnFocus` | boolean | `false` | Select as focus moves. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keep hidden panels in the DOM. |
| `aria-label` | string | – | Names the tab list. |

<Controls of={TabsStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Underline for sections, pills for view switches.** Underline tabs
  sit on a 1px rule and read as the sections of a page; pills sit in a
  `--muted` track and suit a compact "List / Board" switch in a toolbar.
- **Pills keep full-strength labels.** `--muted-foreground` is 4.3:1 on
  the `--muted` track, under the 4.5:1 floor, so every pill label is
  `--foreground` and the selected one is marked by its lifted,
  outlined segment rather than by colour.
- **Selection is manual by default.** Arrow keys move focus; Enter or
  Space selects. That keeps a slow panel from loading on every keypress;
  `activateOnFocus` switches to selecting as you go, for light panels.

## Usage

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Pills} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.FullWidth} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.WithIcons} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Small} />

## Accessibility

- `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and
  `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab.
  Name the list with `aria-label` when no heading does.
- One tab stop: Tab moves into the list and out to the panel; arrows
  move between tabs (Up and Down when vertical), Home and End jump to
  the ends.
- A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is
  found and announced, but it cannot be selected.
- Tabs are 32 or 40px tall and grow to 44px on coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories'

<Meta of={AlertStories} />

# Alert

A message about a page or a section: something went wrong, something
needs attention, something worked. It stays where it is until the
situation changes or the reader dismisses it. For a message that comes
and goes on its own, use a Toast. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithAction} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Icon** | The variant's icon: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`. Replaceable, or `false` for none. |
| **Title** | Optional, semibold. Says what happened in a few words. |
| **Description** | `children`. What it means and what to do. |
| **Action** | Optional buttons or links under the description. |
| **Close button** | Shown when `onClose` is given. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `info` | |
| `appearance` | `subtle`, `outlined`, `solid` | `subtle` | The same three as Tag. |
| `title` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | The description. |
| `icon` | node or `false` | variant's icon | |
| `action` | node | – | |
| `onClose` | function | – | Shows the close button. The alert does not hide itself. |
| `closeLabel` | string | `Dismiss` | The close button's accessible name. |
| `isLive` | boolean | `false` | Announce it when it appears. See Accessibility. |

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={AlertStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The message stays in `--foreground`** on subtle and outlined. A
  paragraph in the variant's text colour is tiring to read, so the colour
  goes on the icon and the title, where the eye lands first.
- **Colours are Tag's.** Each variant reads the same four tokens, e.g.
  `--danger`, `--danger-foreground`, `--danger-subtle`, `--danger-text`,
  so an Alert and a Tag of the same variant always agree.
- **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click; the alert
  is removed by whoever rendered it. That keeps "dismissed" in your state,
  where it can be remembered across visits.

## Usage

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Variants} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Appearances} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithoutIcon} />

## Accessibility

- By default an alert is a plain `<div>`: one that is on the page when it
  loads is read in order, like the text around it.
- An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save)
  needs `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are
  read at once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for
  the screen reader to finish.

  <Canvas of={AlertStories.Live} />

- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`): the variant has to be clear
  from the words too. "Upload failed", not just a red box.
- The close button is named `Dismiss` (change it with `closeLabel`),
  shows the 2px `--ring` on focus, and has a 44px touch target on coarse
  pointers.
- Every variant and appearance is checked for contrast by the story
  tests (light mode).

import * as InlineAlertStories from './InlineAlert.stories'

<Meta of={InlineAlertStories} />

# Inline Alert

A one-line message that sits in the flow of a form or a section: "That
URL is taken", "Changes are saved automatically". No box, no title, no
close button. For a message about a whole page or region, use an
[Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs). Our own spec:
uiguideline.com has no page for it. A plain element.

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Icon** | The variant's icon, one line tall. Replaceable, or `false` for none. |
| **Message** | `children`, in the variant's text colour. |
| **Action** | Optional short link or button after the message. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `info` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | `body-sm` or `body`. |
| `icon` | node or `false` | variant's icon | |
| `action` | node | – | |
| `isLive` | boolean | `false` | Announce it when it appears. |

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={InlineAlertStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The whole line is in the variant's text colour.** Alert can keep its
  message in `--foreground` because the box carries the colour; an
  inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is
  4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays
  readable.
- **Alert or Inline Alert?** Alert when the message is about a page or a
  region and may need a title, an action row or dismissing; Inline Alert
  when it is about the thing right above it.

## Usage

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.InAForm} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.WithAction} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.LongMessage} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Small} />

For an error on a single field, use the field's own `validationState`
and `helperText`: it is tied to the field with `aria-describedby`. Inline
Alert is for messages about a group of fields or a whole form.

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default, read in order with the page.
- `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed
  submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words have to carry the meaning.
