import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ToastStories from './Toast.stories'

<Meta of={ToastStories} />

# Toast

A short message in a corner of the screen about something that just
happened: saved, sent, moved, failed. It closes itself after a few
seconds and never blocks the page. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/toast](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toast).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast).

<Canvas of={ToastStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Icon** | The variant's icon in its text colour; none for `default`, a spinner while a promise is pending. |
| **Title** | Semibold. What happened. |
| **Description** | Optional, `--muted-foreground`. |
| **Action** | Optional, one text button, e.g. "Undo". |
| **Close button** | Always there. |

The surface is `--popover` with `--shadow-lg`, at most 24rem wide.

## API

Wrap the app once in `ToastProvider`, then call `useToast()` anywhere
inside it:

```tsx
<ToastProvider placement="bottom-right">
  <App />
</ToastProvider>

const toast = useToast()
toast.add({ title: 'File moved to Trash', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } })
```

| `ToastProvider` prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `top-` or `bottom-` + `left`, `center`, `right` | `bottom-right` | |
| `timeout` | number (ms) | `5000` | Default time on screen. |
| `limit` | number | `3` | Shown at once; the rest wait. |

| `useToast()` | |
| --- | --- |
| `add(options)` | Shows a toast, returns its id. |
| `update(id, options)` | Changes one in place. |
| `close(id?)` | Closes one, or all. |
| `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` | A loading toast that becomes success or danger when the promise settles. |

| Option | Values | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title`, `description` | node | |
| `variant` | `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | |
| `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | |
| `timeout` | number (ms) | `0` keeps it until dismissed. |
| `priority` | `low`, `high` | `high` by default for `danger`. |
| `onClose` | function | |

<Controls of={ToastStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The variant colours only the icon.** The message stays in
  `--popover-foreground`, the same as Alert's subtle and outlined
  appearances: a toast is read in passing, and body text in an accent
  colour reads worse.
- **Above everything, at z-index 70**, over popups (50) and tooltips
  (60): a toast raised from inside a modal shows over the modal and is
  not hidden from assistive tech by it.

  <Canvas of={ToastStories.FromModal} />

- **Swipe to dismiss** toward the nearest edge on touch.

## Usage

<Canvas of={ToastStories.Variants} />

<Canvas of={ToastStories.PromiseToast} />

<Canvas of={ToastStories.Timeout} />

<Canvas of={ToastStories.TopCenter} />

A toast disappears. Anything the reader must act on, or might need to
read twice, belongs in an Alert on the page or a Modal; the action on a
toast ("Undo") should also be reachable some other way.

## Accessibility

- The viewport is a polite live region: new toasts are announced
  without interrupting. `danger` toasts (and any with `priority: 'high'`)
  are `role="alertdialog"` and announced assertively.
- Each toast is a non-modal dialog named by its title, or by its
  description when it has none (as `promise()` toasts do).
- Timers pause while the pointer is over the toasts or focus is in
  them, so there is time to reach the action. F6 moves focus to the
  toast region.
- The close button is named `Dismiss` and has a 44px touch target on
  coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories'

<Meta of={ModalStories} />

# Modal

A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a
short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed
and out of reach until it closes. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog)
and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog).

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Backdrop** | A black scrim at 50% over the whole page. |
| **Popup** | `--popover` surface, `--shadow-xl`, `--radius-panel`, 24px padding, centred. |
| **Title** | Required. `heading-md`, semibold. Names the dialog. |
| **Close button** | Top right. On by default, off for `isAlert`. |
| **Description** | Optional, `--muted-foreground`. |
| **Body** | `children`. Scrolls when the modal is taller than the screen. |
| **Footer** | Actions, right-aligned, the main one last. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. |
| `trigger` | element | – | Omit when `open` is controlled from elsewhere. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | |
| `footer` | node | – | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | Max width 24, 32, 48rem. |
| `hasCloseButton` | boolean | `!isAlert` | |
| `closeLabel` | string | `Close` | |
| `isAlert` | boolean | `false` | `role="alertdialog"`, no backdrop dismissal. |
| `closeOnBackdropClick` | boolean | `true` | Ignored when `isAlert`. |
| `initialFocus` | ref | – | By default, the first focusable element. |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |

`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with
`render`: `<ModalClose render={<Button />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`.

<Controls of={ModalStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all
  sit at z-index 50. Each portals to the end of `<body>` when it opens,
  so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal lists its
  options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would hide. The
  `WithSelect` story checks it.

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.WithSelect} />

- **The body scrolls, not the page.** Title and footer stay on screen
  however long the content is.

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.Long} />

## Usage

For a decision with consequences, use `isAlert` and say exactly what
will happen in the description. Name the buttons after what they do
("Delete", "Keep project"), not "OK" and "Cancel".

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Alert} />

Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. A Popover suits a
small form tied to one button; an inline message suits information.

## Accessibility

- `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described
  by the description.
- Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`,
  and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer
  events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing
  returns focus to the trigger.
- Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or
  `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its
  own buttons (and Escape).

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.Dismissing} />

- The close button is named `Close`, has the 2px focus ring and a 44px
  touch target on coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories'

<Meta of={PopoverStories} />

# Popover

A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a
share form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click, stays until
you close it, and holds links, inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must
not. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover).

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Open} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | `trigger`: one button. Popover merges its props onto it. |
| **Popup** | `--popover` surface, 1px `--border`, `--shadow-md`, `--radius-panel`, 16px padding, at most 22rem wide. |
| **Title** | Optional. Names the dialog. |
| **Description** | Optional, `--muted-foreground`. Describes the dialog. |
| **Body** | `children`. |
| **Close button** | Optional, in the corner. |
| **Arrow** | Optional. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | element | – | Required. |
| `title` | node | – | Or `aria-label` when there is none. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | |
| `side` | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` | `bottom` | Flips if there is no room. |
| `align` | `start`, `center`, `end` | `center` | |
| `hasArrow` | boolean | `false` | |
| `hasCloseButton` | boolean | `false` | |
| `closeLabel` | string | `Close` | |
| `openOnHover` | boolean | `false` | Also opens on hover, for previews. |
| `isModal` | boolean | `false` | See Accessibility. |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |

<Controls of={PopoverStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Same surface as the Select list.** Popover, Select and Combobox
  popups share the `--popover` colour, border and shadow, and the same
  z-index layer (50); tooltips sit above them at 60.
- **No arrow by default.** The popup opens 6px from its trigger and
  lines up with it; the arrow is there for when the popover could be
  read as belonging to something else nearby.

## Usage

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.ContentOnly} />

## Accessibility

- The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and
  described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-haspopup`.
- Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a click outside closes
  it and returns focus to the trigger.
- **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays
  usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped,
  page scroll is locked and clicks outside are blocked.
- Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a
  touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without
  `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus,
  then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible.

  <Canvas of={PopoverStories.Modal} />

- `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content
  stays reachable by keyboard and touch.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TooltipStories from './Tooltip.stories'

<Meta of={TooltipStories} />

# Tooltip

A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the
name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, a one-line hint. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/tooltip](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tooltip).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip).

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.LongContent} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | `children`: one focusable element. Tooltip merges its props onto it rather than wrapping it. |
| **Popup** | Inverted: `--foreground` behind `--background` text, `body-sm`, at most 20rem wide. |
| **Arrow** | Optional, points at the trigger. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | node | – | Required. |
| `children` | element | – | Required. The trigger. |
| `side` | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` | `top` | Flips if there is no room. |
| `align` | `start`, `center`, `end` | `center` | |
| `delay` | number (ms) | `600` | Hover delay. Focus opens it at once. |
| `closeDelay` | number (ms) | `0` | |
| `hasArrow` | boolean | `true` | |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Never opens. |

`TooltipGroup` (Base UI's `Tooltip.Provider`) wraps several tooltips so
that once one has opened, moving to the next opens it without the delay:

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.Group} />

<Controls of={TooltipStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Inverted in both modes.** A tooltip is not part of the page; the
  dark-on-light (light-on-dark in dark mode) box says so, at the same
  contrast as body text.
- **600ms before it opens on hover.** Shorter and tooltips flash as the
  pointer crosses a toolbar; `TooltipGroup` removes the wait once the
  reader is clearly browsing tooltips.

## Usage

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.WithoutArrow} />

Only one tooltip is open at a time: opening one closes any other. Hover
or focus the triggers above to see them.

Keep it to a label or a hint. Anything a reader needs in order to finish
a task belongs on the page: a tooltip cannot be reached by touch, and it
disappears the moment you look away. For interactive content, use a
Popover.

## Accessibility

- It opens on hover after `delay` and on keyboard focus at once, and
  closes on Escape, blur or pointer leave.
- Base UI keeps tooltips out of the accessibility tree. This component
  gives the popup `role="tooltip"` and, while it is open, points the
  trigger's `aria-describedby` at it, so it is read as a description.
- It is a **description, not a name.** An icon-only button still needs
  its own `aria-label`; the tooltip then shows that label to sighted
  users too.
- The trigger must be focusable. A disabled button is not, so its
  tooltip never opens by keyboard: put the reason it is disabled in text
  next to it instead.
- Hover and touch cannot reach the tooltip content, so it must never hold
  a link or a button.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories'

<Meta of={EmptyStateStories} />

# Empty State

What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet:
why it is empty, and what to do about it. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/empty-state](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/empty-state).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Icon** | Optional. An icon on a `--muted` disc, or a small illustration. Decorative. |
| **Title** | A real heading, level set by `headingLevel`. Says what is empty. |
| **Description** | Optional, `--muted-foreground`, at most 40 characters wide. Says why, or what will appear here. |
| **Action** | Optional. The way forward: usually one Button, at most two. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `icon` | node | – | |
| `action` | node | – | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | `sm` for a panel or a table body. |
| `headingLevel` | 2–6 | `2` | |

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={EmptyStateStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Three kinds of empty, three kinds of copy.** First use ("No projects
  yet", with a way to create one), no results ("No projects match", with
  a way to clear the filter) and cleared out ("All caught up", often
  with no action at all). The component is the same; the words are not.
- **The icon sits on a disc** rather than floating alone, so an empty
  area gets a centre of gravity without needing an illustration.

## Usage

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.TitleOnly} />

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading, so a screen reader user jumping by headings
  finds out the area is empty. Set `headingLevel` to fit the outline:
  `3` inside a section headed by an `h2`.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title has to say it all.
- An empty state that replaces results after a search is not announced by
  itself. If the search updates as you type, announce the count
  elsewhere (a `role="status"` line such as "0 results").

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ErrorStateStories from './ErrorState.stories'

<Meta of={ErrorStateStories} />

# Error State

What a list, a panel or a page shows when loading it failed: what went
wrong, and a way forward, usually "Try again". Our own spec:
uiguideline.com has no page for it. Built on
[Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs), in the
danger tone.

<Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.WithDetails} />

## Anatomy

Empty State's parts (icon disc, title, description, action), plus:

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Icon disc** | `--danger-subtle` behind the `danger` icon in `--danger-text`. |
| **Details** | Optional, under the description: an error code or request id, monospaced and selectable in one click. |

## Props

Every Empty State prop (`icon`, `description`, `action`, `size`,
`headingLevel`), and:

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | `Something went wrong` | |
| `details` | node | – | |
| `isLive` | boolean | `false` | `role="alert"`. |

<Controls of={ErrorStateStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Say what failed and that nothing is lost.** "Couldn’t load projects.
  Your projects are safe" beats "Error". The default title is the last
  resort, for failures you cannot describe.
- **Details are for support, not for the reader.** Keep them small and
  selectable so they can be pasted into a message.

## Usage

<Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.DefaultTitle} />

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading, as on Empty State.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="alert"`: use it when the error replaces
  content that was loading, so a screen reader hears that it failed.

  <Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.Live} />

- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says it.

# Success State

What a flow shows when it has finished: the invites are sent, the import

- **A success state ends a flow; a Toast confirms an action.** Use this

import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AppShellStories from './AppShell.stories'

<Meta of={AppShellStories} />

# App Shell

The frame of an application: navigation, a header, and the page. The
navigation stays put while the page scrolls, and on a phone it moves into
a drawer that the header's menu button opens. Four pieces: `AppShell`,
`AppHeader`, `AppNav` for top navigation, and the kit's
[Sidebar](?path=/docs/components-navigation-sidebar--docs).

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/app-shell.json
```

## With sidebar

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithSidebar} />

## Collapsed rail

Sidebar's `isCollapsible` turns it into an icon rail that the reader can
expand. The links keep their names, and show them as tooltips.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.CollapsedRail} />

## Top navigation

No sidebar: a logo and `AppNav` links in the header. `mobileNavigation`
says what the drawer holds on a phone, where the links move.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopNavigation} />

## On a phone

Under 64rem of shell width (48rem for top navigation) the navigation is a
drawer. The header gets a menu button that opens it; choosing a link or
pressing Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.Mobile} />

## Props

**AppShell**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sidebar` | node | – | A Sidebar. Beside the content from 64rem, in the drawer below. |
| `header` | node | – | An AppHeader. |
| `mobileNavigation` | node | `sidebar` | What the drawer holds. |
| `navigationLabel` | string | `Navigation` | Names the drawer and its buttons. |
| `mainId` | string | generated | The `id` of the `main` element, the skip link's target. |
| `children` | node | – | The page, inside `<main>`. |

`sidebar={isAdmin && <Sidebar … />}` works: `false` and `null` count as
no sidebar, so there is no empty column, no drawer and no menu button.

**AppHeader** takes `start` (breadcrumbs, or a logo and AppNav), `end`
(search, notifications, the account menu) and `children` for the middle.

**AppNav** takes `items` (`{ label, href }[]`) and `currentHref`.

## Layout

- **The shell fills the viewport** (`block-size: 100dvh`) and its content
  column scrolls, so the sidebar and the sticky header stay in place. Set
  `block-size` on it to put it in a smaller box.
- **Breakpoints are the shell's own width**, which in an app is the
  viewport's. That is also what lets the stories show the phone layout in
  a 390px box.
- **The shell is a size container** (`container-type: inline-size`), so
  it takes its width from where it sits, never from its content. In a
  block it fills the line as usual; as a flex or grid item that would
  otherwise shrink to fit, give it a width (`inline-size: 100%` or
  `flex: 1`), or it collapses.
- **The drawer holds the same Sidebar.** A collapsible one opens there
  as the icon rail if it is collapsed, so for a collapsed rail pass a
  plain Sidebar as `mobileNavigation`.

## Accessibility

- A "Skip to content" link is the first thing in the shell, visible when
  focused. It moves focus past the navigation to the `main` element. Give
  `mainId` when something else should link there too; otherwise the id is
  generated, so two shells in one page (as in these docs) never share it.
- The page is the `main` landmark; the sidebar and AppNav are `nav`
  landmarks named "Main". Only one is in the page at a time: the hidden
  one is `display: none`, so it is out of the accessibility tree too.
- The drawer is a modal dialog named "Navigation": focus moves into it,
  the page behind is inert, and Escape closes it. The menu button says
  so with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
- The drawer slides in from the start edge, from the right in a
  right-to-left page. It is portalled to the body, so it reads the page's
  direction: set `dir="rtl"` on `<html>`, not only on the shell.

import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DataTablePageStories from './DataTablePage.stories'

<Meta of={DataTablePageStories} />

# Data Table Page

A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs),
what is shown and the pages below it, and, while rows are selected, what
you can do with them. Two pieces, `TableToolbar` (with
`TableToolbarGroup`) and `TableFooter`, around the kit's Table, Search,
Select and Pagination. Filtering, paging and the data are yours: the
stories show one way to wire them.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/data-table-page.json
```

## Toolbar and pagination

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.ToolbarAndPagination} />

## Bulk actions

With `selectedCount` above zero the toolbar swaps its tools for the
selection's actions and a "Clear selection" button, on the accent
surface so the change of mode is visible.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.BulkActions} />

## Empty result

When nothing matches, the Table's `emptyState` says so and offers the way
back; the footer goes away.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.EmptyResult} />

## Props

**TableToolbar**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | node | – | Search, filters, the primary action. |
| `selectedCount` | number | `0` | From 1, the selection bar replaces the children. |
| `selectionActions` | node | – | |
| `onClearSelection` | function | – | Shows "Clear selection". |
| `selectionLabel` | `(n) => string` | `"{n} selected"` | |

`TableToolbarGroup` wraps the part that should take the free space and
wrap first, usually the search and filters.

**TableFooter** takes `summary` ("Showing 1–5 of 12") and, as children,
usually a Pagination.

## Behaviour to copy

- **Filtering returns to page 1.** A new query on page 3 would otherwise
  show an empty page, or a page the reader never asked for.
- **Selection is by id**, so it survives sorting and paging (Table's
  `getRowId`), and an action clears it once it has been applied.
- Both bars wrap: on a phone the search takes its own line and the
  filters and action flow under it.

## Accessibility

- The selection count is a polite status line that is always in the page,
  so "2 selected" is announced as it changes, and silence when it clears.
- Search and the status filter are named ("Search projects", "Status")
  without visible labels, since the table's caption and placeholder make
  their purpose clear on screen.
- The empty state is a heading inside the table's body, so a screen reader
  reaching the table hears why it is empty.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DescriptionListStories from './DescriptionList.stories'

<Meta of={DescriptionListStories} />

# Description List

The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order,
an application. It is read-only; its editable twin is a settings form in
Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/description-list.json
```

## Columns

Term and details side by side, a line between rows, and an optional
action at the end of each row ("Update").

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## In a card

`isCard` puts the header in a top band and the list below it, inside one
border. With `layout="grid"`, fields run two to a row; `isWide` gives
long text and attachments the full width.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.InCard} />

## Stacked

Term over details, one field after another: for a sidebar or a narrow
panel.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Stacked} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `DescriptionItem[]` | – | Required. `{ term, details, action?, isWide? }` |
| `title` | node | – | |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons at the end of the header. |
| `layout` | `columns`, `grid`, `stacked` | `columns` | |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

<Controls of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## Layout

- **It responds to its own width, not the viewport's.** Columns and grid
  are container queries: under 36rem of list width they stack, so the
  same list works in a main column, a sidebar and a phone.

  <Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.ColumnsNarrow} />

- Details wrap anywhere, so a long email address or URL never pushes the
  layout wide.

## Accessibility

- A real `<dl>`: a screen reader announces a list of terms and reads each
  detail with its term.
- Row actions sit in their own `<dd>` after the details. Give each one the
  field it acts on ("Update Email address"), hidden if you like, so a
  list of links is not six identical "Update"s.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FormLayoutsStories from './FormLayouts.stories'

<Meta of={FormLayoutsStories} />

# Form Layouts

How the kit's fields are arranged into a form: sections with a heading
and a line of context, fields one or two to a row, and a row of actions
at the end. Three pieces: `FormSection`, `FormFullWidth` and
`FormActions`. The `<form>` element is yours.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/form-layouts.json
```

## Settings sections

A settings page. Each section's title and description sit in a column
beside its fields, sections are separated by a line, and one row of
actions saves the lot.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.SettingsSections} />

## Stacked in a card

One section on a card: the title above, fields two to a row, and the
actions in the card's bottom band.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.StackedInCard} />

## In a modal

A short form in a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).
The submit button sits in the modal's footer, outside the `<form>`, and
points at it with the `form` attribute, so Enter in a field and a click on
the button both submit.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.InModal} />

## FormSection props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. An `h2` by default. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | The fields. Give each input `isFullWidth`. |
| `layout` | `split`, `stacked` | `split` | Split puts the intro in a column beside the fields. |
| `columns` | `1`, `2` | `1` | Two fields to a row. Wrap one in `FormFullWidth` to span the row. |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `footer` | node | – | Usually `FormActions`; the card's bottom band when `isCard`. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

`FormActions` is a row of buttons aligned to the end: secondary actions
first, the primary one last.

<Controls of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

## Layout

- **Sections respond to their own width.** Split turns into stacked under
  48rem of section width, and two columns into one when the fields' side
  of the section (its whole width once stacked) is under 32rem. A form in
  a sidebar or a phone needs no extra props.
- **Sections are size containers**, so they take their width from where
  they sit. As a flex or grid item that would shrink to fit, give the
  section a width (`inline-size: 100%`), or it collapses.

  <Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

- Actions end-aligned, primary last: the same place in every form, where
  the eye and the Tab key end up.

## Accessibility

- Each section is a `<section>` with a heading, so the form's parts are in
  the page outline and a screen reader can jump between them.
- Group related checkboxes in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, as the
  Notifications section does; RadioGroup does this for you.
- Mark required fields with `required`. The field shows the asterisk and
  the browser enforces it; say in the description if most fields are
  optional instead.
- Never disable the submit button to show that a form is incomplete. Let
  it submit, and show what is missing next to each field.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PageHeadingStories from './PageHeading.stories'

<Meta of={PageHeadingStories} />

# Page Heading

The top of a page: where it is, what it is, and what you can do with it.
Breadcrumbs, title, a line of description, a few facts, the page's
actions, and optionally tabs for sections of the same page.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/page-heading.json
```

## Simple

Title, description and the page's main actions. Keep it to one primary
action; everything else is secondary.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.Simple} />

## With breadcrumbs and meta

A record's page. Breadcrumbs say where it sits; meta holds short facts,
each optionally led by an icon or a Tag for a status. Rarely used actions
go in a Menu behind "More actions" so the row stays short.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.WithBreadcrumbsAndMeta} />

## With tabs

Sections of the same page as Tabs under the heading. The tab list's line
replaces the heading's own bottom border.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.WithTabs} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. |
| `description` | node | – | Muted, capped at 65 characters a line. |
| `breadcrumbs` | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | – | Rendered small, above the title. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode[]` | – | A list of short facts. |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons, a Menu. |
| `tabs` | node | – | A `Tabs` element. |
| `headingLevel` | `1`, `2` | `1` | 2 when the heading sits inside a larger page. |

Every other `<header>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={PageHeadingStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- **Actions wrap, the title does not squeeze.** The title takes the row
  down to 20rem, then the actions drop underneath it, keeping their order.
  On a phone that means title first, then buttons.

  <Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.Narrow} />

- **Long titles break anywhere** rather than overflow, so a record named
  with one long word still fits.

## Accessibility

- The title is the page's `h1` by default. A page has one; pass
  `headingLevel={2}` if the heading sits under another.
- Breadcrumbs are a `nav` named "Breadcrumb", with the current page
  marked `aria-current="page"`.
- Meta is a list, so a screen reader announces how many facts there are.
  Icons in it are decorative; say the fact in words ("12 applicants").
- An icon-only action needs an `aria-label`, as on any Button.

import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StatsStories from './Stats.stories'

<Meta of={StatsStories} />

# Stats

Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and
optionally how it moved since the last period, an icon, and a link to
the details. The top of a dashboard or a report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stats.json
```

## Simple

<Canvas of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## With trend

`previous` gives the figure to compare against; `change` says by how
much and which way. The colour follows whether the change is good news,
not its direction: pass `isPositive: true` for figures where down is
good, like churn or response time.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithTrend} />

## With icon and link

An icon on a rounded square of the primary colour, and a link at the foot of each
card to where the figure comes from.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithIconAndLink} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `Stat[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `title` | node | – | A heading above the cards. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

Each `Stat` has `label`, `value`, and optionally `previous`, `change`
(`{ value, direction: 'up' \| 'down', isPositive? }`), `icon`, `href` and
`linkLabel` (default "View all").

<Controls of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- As many 14rem columns as fit: three or four on a desktop, one on a
  phone. Cards in a row share a height.

  <Canvas of={StatsStories.Narrow} />

- Figures use tabular numbers, so a row of values lines up digit by digit
  and does not jitter when it updates.

## Accessibility

- A definition list: each figure is the definition of its label, so a
  screen reader reads "Total subscribers, 71,897".
- The change is read as words ("Increased by 12%"), not only shown as an
  arrow and a colour. The colours are `--success-text` and `--danger-text`
  on their subtle surfaces, 4.5:1 in both appearances.
- Each "View all" link carries its figure's label for screen readers
  ("View all Avg. open rate"), so a list of links is not three identical
  entries.
- The icon is decorative.
